ownerThemes.theme: A PatternReview owner who moved from domestic machines for bag making notes she no longer hand cranks through bulky seams; another says the servo motor makes speed very controllable.

New-to-industrial buyers on PatternReview ask whether the DDL-8700 can be sewn slowly and whether it will hold up to leather coats; replies steer them to servo motors and to the -H heavy variant for thick work.
Quiltingboard members recommend the servo motor and point out the head takes standard high shank feet, with bobbins and needles easy to buy online.
A Backpacking Light thread covers upgrading a clutch-motor 8700 to a servo for quieter, slower gear sewing.

editorial.verdict: Straight-stitch industrial head that Juki classes as medium-weight: owners praise the build, but it needs a table, a motor and floor space, and heavy leather is -H territory.
editorial.whoFor: Bag makers, gear sewers and small production shops who sew straight seams all day and want speed, a knee lift and an oil-bath hook.
editorial.skipIf: You need a portable machine, any stitch besides straight, or you expect it to sew heavy leather; Juki positions the DDL-8700H variant for heavy weight.
editorial.keySpec: 5,500 spm (base) · straight stitch · DBx1 needle · table + motor required
strengths: Owners report solid build and smooth running, with 6 of 7 build-quality voices positive.
Retailer reviewers often call it quiet; Juki's manual gives 83.5 dB(A) at 5,000 sti/min, a maker figure on paper.
Owners report standard feet, bobbins and DBx1 needles are easy to buy, and a free-motion foot worked for one owner.
weaknesses: Owners report recurring tension trouble, such as top thread showing underneath, though many of these are help-seeking Reddit threads.
Owners report setup and defect problems, such as a motor that ran backward at first and a bobbin that bunched when the needle did not stop up.
Owners report limits on thick or slippery work: one gets two layers of heavy waxed denim but thread snaps at three, and another could not sew split leather.

faqs.q: Does the Juki DDL-8700 come with a table and motor?
faqs.a: Not from the maker: it is sold as a head only. Dealer bundles add a table, stand and a clutch or servo motor, so check what a listing includes.

faqs.q: Should I get a servo motor or a clutch motor?
faqs.a: Owners on Quiltingboard and Backpacking Light recommend a servo for slow, controllable sewing, and the servo has a speed dial under the table.

faqs.q: Can the Juki DDL-8700 sew leather?
faqs.a: Owner reports are mixed: a tailor sewed vegetable-tanned leather to suede on the base machine, while another owner could not sew split leather. Juki positions the DDL-8700H as the heavy-weight variant.

faqs.q: How fast is it and can it be slowed down?
faqs.a: Juki lists 5,500 stitches per minute for the base DDL-8700; the DDL-8700A and DDL-8700H are 4,000. Slow control depends on the motor, and owners point to a servo.

faqs.q: What needles does the base DDL-8700 use?
faqs.a: Juki's page lists DB x 1 in sizes 9 to 18, with 14 as standard. The DDL-8700A uses DA x 1 and the DDL-8700H uses DB x 1 in sizes 19 to 23.
Juki describes automatic lubrication of the hook with a sealed oil pan, and its manual names Juki New Defrix Oil No. 1.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the DDL-8700, -7 and -H?
faqs.a: Per Juki's page the base is medium-weight at 5,500 spm and the H is heavy-weight at 4,000 spm. The -7 is the trimmer variant per dealer sources, and listings often mix them up.

faqs.q: Does it use home sewing machine feet?
faqs.a: Quiltingboard members say the head takes standard high shank feet, and one Reddit owner reports a $30 free-motion foot worked very well.
Juki does not publish a weight in its page or manual, so we show [verify]. A table and motor add to the head weight.
